title: Visible internals
subtitle: A frosted enclosure with monochrome e-ink.
paragraphs: I began with a paper prototype for a frosted plastic enclosure. The concept would keep the internal components visible, with a monochrome e-ink display providing participant feedback.
modelLabel: Design 7 enclosure model shown as a placeholder for Design 1

title: A kitchen appliance direction
subtitle: A bulkier form with a backlit LCD.
paragraphs: I explored a much bulkier form with the character of a kitchen appliance. This direction used a dual-colour backlit LCD as the proposed feedback display.
modelLabel: Design 7 enclosure model shown as a placeholder for Design 2

title: A thin display and heavier base
subtitle: A miniature all-in-one computer.
paragraphs: I paired a very thin e-ink display with a heavier base intended to house the computing hardware. I approached it like a miniature all-in-one computer, with the screen and computing components occupying different areas of the same object.
modelLabel: Design 7 enclosure model shown as a placeholder for Design 3

title: The structure takes shape
subtitle: An angled display and layered internals.
paragraphs: Design 4 established the direction around a 4.26-inch e-ink display, a Raspberry Pi 4 behind it and a kickstand to set the viewing angle. I explored a clear acrylic front inspired by the iMac G4, but bonding the display to it with resin was difficult to achieve and repeat.

The internal sandwich structure carried into later designs, along with the ISS-inspired part names. The Integrated Truss Structure supported the Pi and display and provided routes for the USB-C and RJ45 cables.
modelLabel: Design 7 enclosure model shown as a placeholder for Design 4

title: Connections built in
subtitle: A remodelled enclosure with cables through the stand.
paragraphs: I remodelled the exterior using what I had learned from Design 4. A frosted acrylic label at the upper rear held the hardware information and serial number.
Feedback from the first pilot led me to incorporate built-in cables exiting through the rear stand. Participants wanted to avoid having to choose and connect the wrong cables.
modelLabel: Design 7 enclosure model shown as a placeholder for Design 5

title: Refining the build
subtitle: Printability, cost and a slimmer branch.
paragraphs: Design 6 stayed close to Design 5. I focused on printability and the bill of materials, removing the acrylic rear label strip because of cost. I also made a few hubs for firmware development and continued exploring the packaging.
revisionNote: Within Design 6, the frame became slimmer around revision 6.3. The asymmetric branch I called Design 6.4 Slim prompted further work on the internal arrangement.
modelLabel: Design 7 enclosure model shown as a placeholder for Design 6

title: The final thin frame
subtitle: A symmetrical form with repackaged internals.
paragraphs: The slim branch led to Design 7, the final design with a symmetrical thin frame. I reworked the internal arrangement through repeated small dimensional adjustments to make the parts fit within the slimmer form.
